page.layout: One page of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: sacra Domini Cœna, quibus primùm ineptiis ac tandem impietatibus sit profanata, quis satis possit deplorare? quas impurissimas fordes, mihi religio est pluribus contrectare. Sed ista certè quantumuis horrenda satis execrari, nec possumus, nec debemus: quòd nimirùm signis illis sacris in ipsummet Christum transmutatis, sacra hæc Cœna (idcirco instituta ut adhibita solenni mortis Christi annuntiatione, & gratiarum actione, illius nobiscum communio intra nos sanciatur) sit in idolomaniam, qua nihil unquam indignius Sol aspexit, ac tandem ex Sacramento in sacrificium expiatorium, idque pro vivis & mortuis, transformata. Et utinā videant qui in tanta Euangelij luce adhuc ἐπιδείξιν[?] & alia nō dissimilia retinent, à quibus certum est cœpisse illius adorationis βδέλυγμα, quàm prudenter sibi & posteris suis caveant. Viderint quoque Consubstantiatores, præsertim Vbiquitarij, annon tantorum malorum semen & fomitem retineant. Sed de istis sordibus plus satis, de quibus ne cogitare quidem sine horrore verè pij omnes possunt, quantacunque antiquitatis specie fucatis.

MinùsErrores eorum, qui minus sacramentis tribuunt quàm deceat. autem multò quàm par sit Sacra-mentis tribuunt, qui, neglectis quæ ad ordi-nem, & sanctam quandam in omni diuino cultu obseruandam reuerentiam faciunt, sacras istas actiones irreuerenter, & non aliter quàm res communes & quotidianas exercét.

page.notes: Greek word "ἐπιδείξιν" in the line "adhuc ... & alia" is hard to read at the scan resolution; the accents and letters are doubtful. Marked [?]. The first word "sacra" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The marginal note is set in small type on the right and runs three lines with hyphenation ("eo-rum", "sa-cramentis", "de-ceat"), which was joined. Long s was rendered as plain s, and the printed "fanciatur" was read as "sanciatur". Printed spelling such as "viuis" was changed to "vivis" and "vtiná" to "utinā" by the u/v rule.
